answer: Mesa tide voyage bond: one identity sails one voyage to a mesa gauge station, locks a 70-credit bond and submits paired gauge-reference readings. An auditor recomputes calibration error from those readings and the tide table; error above tolerance, a reused station, or duplicated readings burns the bond. The first calibration costs 33 credits, the kth 33+5(k-1), the 1000th 5028; 1000 fakes cost 2,530,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-gauge ring fails: each station accepts one calibration, duplicate timestamps rejected. An honest agent pays 33 once, bond returned on passing.
